Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · Detailed Summary

Class features.
Built into the roll.

Class abilities connected to your native attacks, damage rolls, saves, and chat cards.

Automations → Unique Classes

Your class abilities,
right when you need them.

Choose your smite, unleash a maneuver, or add your class’s extra damage as you make the attack. Relevant options appear in the roll, with a preview of the damage you’re about to deal. The module tracks supported resources and once-per-turn uses, helping players focus on their next move and giving the GM less to keep track of. Explore the class sections below to see what’s supported.

Barbarian

Barbarians live to attack. With so many features triggered by an attack or damage roll, going back to add dice or adjust results can get confusing. Now those choices are built right into your Attack and Damage rolls—choose your strike, add your damage, and keep the fight moving.

  • Reckless Attack On your first attack, use Reckless above Advantage to apply the native effect and roll. Strength attacks gain advantage until your next turn; attacks against you also gain advantage. Disadvantage combines normally.
  • Frenzy While Rage and Reckless are active, the first qualifying Strength-based weapon hit on your turn includes the configured damage rider, with critical support.
  • Zealot · Divine Fury While raging, your first weapon or Unarmed Strike hit on your turn adds 1d6 plus half your Barbarian level. Choose Radiant or Necrotic in damage Configuration; the dice roll with the initial damage and support critical hits.
  • Zealot · Fanatical Focus A failed-save card offers one replacement d20 plus your Rage Damage bonus, once per active Rage. Previous advantage/disadvantage is not reused; the new result is mandatory. Recorded targeting is restored after the reroll.
  • Zealot · Zealous Presence Recipients gain advantage on attacks and saves until the start of the source Barbarian’s next turn. Attacking does not consume it; other sources and AC5E combine normally.
  • Brutal Strike Use Brutal above Normal for a Strength attack on your turn without disadvantage. It activates Reckless on your first attack or reuses active Reckless later, forgoes advantage, and uses your one chosen Brutal attack for the turn even on a miss.
  • Brutal effects in damage Configuration Hits include scaled Brutal damage with the weapon roll. Choose Forceful or Hamstring Blow; Improved Brutal Strike adds Staggering and Sundering, and Improved Brutal Strike (2) allows two different effects. Native Hamstrung, Staggered, and Sundered effects apply to hit targets, expire at your next turn start, and support Apply/Undo. Movement stays manual.
  • Sundered The next single-target attack by someone other than the source Barbarian gains +5, once, then consumes eligible Sundered effects whether it hits or misses. Canceling the prompt preserves the effect.
  • Staggered The next saving throw has disadvantage through AC5E or the standalone flow. Magic Resistance advantage cancels it to Normal. After that save, the native effect stays until expiry for its Opportunity Attack restriction.

Bard

Bards live to inspire. They live to taunt. Adding your dice to an existing roll no longer means working it out afterward. Prompts appear directly on eligible rolls, only when you have the resources to spend, and automatically use the right die size.

  • Bardic Inspiration Inspire automatically applies the configured Inspired effect and records the source Bard’s die. A failed attack, save, or ability check can add that die without rerolling the original d20. Rolling spends the grant; unknown-DC tests request confirmation or a DC.
  • Lore · Cutting Words Eligible enemy attack-hit and damage cards offer Cutting Words within 60 feet, with a Reaction and Inspiration use available. Original dice remain; damage components are selectable and cannot fall below zero. Sight walls block eligibility and users confirm visibility. Undo applied damage before adjusting it.
  • Lore · Peerless Skill Add your current Inspiration die to your own failed attack or ability check. The original roll stays; the resource is spent only when the adjusted test succeeds.
  • Valor · Combat Inspiration damage A default-No damage Configuration choice adds the granted Inspiration die to the initial attack damage, including criticals. Confirming spends Inspired; canceling preserves it.
  • Valor · Combat Inspiration defense An incoming hit offers the recipient a Reaction to add the granted die to AC against that attack. It combines with Shield and consumes the existing Inspired grant rather than another use from the Bard.

Fighter · Battle Master

Battle Masters live for the fight. Choose maneuvers at the point of use in damage Configuration, with attack and damage card actions where needed. No awkward updates or manual dice rerolls—pick your maneuver, take the shot, and keep the fight moving.

Learned maneuvers use Combat Superiority’s available charges and the character’s current die, including d10 and d12 progression. One maneuver can be used per attack. Damage riders join the weapon’s roll and support critical hits.

  • Precision Attack A missed attack card offers Precision Attack. Add the Superiority Die to the original attack without rerolling its d20. Undo applied damage before correcting an attack.
  • Trip Attack Adds damage and prompts a Strength save for Large or smaller targets. Failure toggles the native Prone condition, compatible with standard condition controls and Automated Conditions 5e.
  • Distracting Strike Adds damage and grants advantage to the next attack by a creature other than the Fighter. The effect clears after that attack or at the start of the Fighter’s next turn.
  • Menacing Attack Adds damage and prompts a Wisdom save. Failure applies native Frightened, linked to the Fighter until the end of their next turn.
  • Goading Attack Adds damage and prompts a Wisdom save. Failure causes disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than the Fighter until the end of the Fighter’s next turn. Existing advantage cancels that disadvantage normally.
  • Maneuvering Attack Adds the current Superiority Die to damage and a reminder tag. Choosing the ally, spending their reaction, and moving remain manual.
  • Pushing Attack Adds damage and prompts a Strength save for Large or smaller targets. The card reminds the GM to resolve a failed save’s push of up to 15 feet directly away; movement remains manual.
  • Relentless Characters with the feature gain a Superiority Die dropdown beneath Maneuver. Spend the current die by default, or select d8 — Free (Relentless). The free use is shared across maneuvers, including Precision Attack, once per active combat turn. It becomes available on the next creature’s turn, allowing a qualifying reaction maneuver. With no normal dice left, the free d8 is selected when available. Canceling does not spend it.
  • Cards, effects, and settings Reminder tags identify Goading, Maneuvering, Pushing, and Relentless. Applicable effects retain Apply/Undo controls. Find individual maneuver and Relentless settings under Automations → Unique Classes → Fighter.
  • Parry Incoming single-target melee damage cards offer Parry when a Reaction and Superiority Die are available. It reduces the existing damage, spends the die, and marks the Reaction used. Undo already-applied damage first.

Great Weapon Fighting and Great Weapon Master are under Feats. Other maneuvers remain manual.

Monk

Strike hard. Strike fast. Masters of unarmed combat, Monks move quickly and attack just as fast. Choose Stunning Strike and Grapple right in damage Configuration, keeping those decisions together at the actual damage roll so you can keep the fight moving.

  • Stunning Strike On a qualifying Monk-weapon or Unarmed Strike hit, damage Configuration offers a default-No choice. Confirming Yes spends 1 Focus Point and prompts the native Constitution save, once per combat turn.
  • Failed and successful saves Failure applies Stunned. Success halves Speed and grants advantage on the next attack against the creature. These effects last until the start of the Monk’s next turn.
  • Stun before Grapple When combined with Grapple, Stunning Strike resolves first, including its animation and automatic effects. A Stunned target automatically fails the following Strength/Dexterity save.
  • Independent corrections Undo Effect restores the Apply control and unlocks Stunning Strike’s rolled save adjustments independently of weapon damage. Reapplication locks its save again.

Shared Grapple / Prone prompts are under Common; Grappler’s feat benefits have their own Feats setting.

Paladin

Holy warriors. Masters of the smite. Focus on landing that critical hit, not juggling extra buttons. Divine Smite and supported prepared Smite spells are built into damage Configuration, so you can choose your smite where the damage happens and bring divine judgment down on your enemies.

  • Divine Smite Eligible melee weapon hit damage offers the feature’s available free cast or a spell-slot selection. The chosen resource and bonus action are consumed; slot-funded casts also use the character spell-slot tracker.
  • Fiend and Undead bonus A golden glow and underline indicate that the target qualifies for an extra d8. The info icon explains the bonus. Damage scales with the selected slot and follows the attack’s critical damage.
  • Prepared Smite spells Choose a supported prepared 2024 Smite spell in damage Configuration instead of Divine Smite. Its initial damage joins the weapon’s roll and follows the critical result. The selected slot/free use and bonus action are spent once.
  • Saves and effects Only Smites requiring a save create a separate save card. Their effects apply on failure, or directly when no save is needed, under the existing application settings. A Smite tag on the damage card shows your choice. Lingering damage and saves use the creature-trigger library.

Ranger

Stalk your prey. Know your prey. Hunt your prey. Let the system help track your bonus damage, with Hunter’s Mark and Hunter’s Prey built into damage Configuration. Keep your focus on the hunt while eligible riders join the attack’s damage roll.

  • Hunter’s Prey / Colossus Slayer Adds the configured extra damage against an injured single target, once per combat turn. The selector initially defaults to No and remembers the previous choice. Full-health targets disable it; damage matches the weapon and supports criticals.

Hunter’s Mark is grouped with Spells because its rider follows the caster’s concentration and marked target.

Rogue

  • Sneak Attack Damage Configuration defaults to Yes after an attack with advantage and No otherwise. The player or GM can select it when another qualifying circumstance applies; this is assistance, not a complete eligibility ruling.
  • Damage and timing Uses the feature’s configured damage and the weapon’s damage type, including critical support. The once-per-turn marker resets at the end of the current combat turn, allowing a later qualifying reaction attack. Canceling does not consume it.

Sorcerer

Pure magic, embodied. Control the battlefield, transmute your spells, and overpower your enemies with raw magical force. Let the system handle Metamagic choices during casting and carry them into damage, keeping those decisions connected to the spell instead of managing extra cards afterward.

  • Innate Sorcery While its effect is active, Sorcerer spell attacks recommend advantage. Other classes’ spells and weapon attacks are excluded; other advantage/disadvantage sources still combine normally.
  • Transmuted Spell Choose an eligible elemental damage type before rolling. The choice follows subsequent damage from that casting, with no repeated Sorcery Point charge.
  • Heightened Spell Choose one target before its save. Disadvantage combines with other sources, so Magic Resistance can cancel it to a normal save.
  • Careful Spell Select protected creatures before rolling. It records automatic successes and prevents half-on-save damage for those creatures. Protection does not remove targets from a nonselective spell.
  • Empowered Spell The spell damage card offers a feature-icon action. Select active damage dice up to the Charisma modifier, minimum one, then confirm to spend 1 Sorcery Point and keep the new results, even when lower. Opening the picker hands automatic application back to manual control; applied damage must first be undone.
  • Seeking Spell A missed spell attack offers a reroll action. Spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll one d20 and use the new result; linked hit/critical results update, with a damage prompt on a hit.
  • Costs, combinations, and card tags Cast-time choices respect supported Sorcery Incarnate / active Innate Sorcery combination limits and Arcane Apotheosis free-use accounting. Empowered and Seeking remain result-card options. Tags show the applied Metamagic, with element and target details in tooltips.

Warlock

  • Eldritch Smite An eligible pact-weapon hit offers a default-No damage rider. Yes spends a Pact Magic slot, scales Force damage with that slot’s level, and marks the feature used for the combat turn. It does not consume a bonus action.

Hex, Conjure Minor Elementals, and the Eldritch Blast remaining-attacks window are described under Spells.
